# sngl:internal/ is the compiler's own tier: the URI set, what each package
# holds, and whether a package exists at all are implementation details.
#
# Importable from a program, the marks package let user source stamp
# #[intrinsic("...")] on its own function. That checked clean and then panicked
# in codegen — RequireIntrinsicFallback, because no backend can implement a name
# it has never heard of. This is a txtar rather than a fixture because the
# checker's testdata harness reports only a fixture's own diagnostics.

! sngl check marks.sngl
stderr 'internal to the compiler and cannot be imported'
! stderr 'unknown internal package'

! sngl check draw.sngl
stderr 'internal to the compiler and cannot be imported'

# The panic this closes: with the import allowed, the intrinsic reached codegen.
! sngl generate --platform html --lang none -o out intrinsic.sngl
stderr 'internal to the compiler and cannot be imported'
! stderr 'panic'

# lib/ still reaches its own tier — draw is written against internal/draw, and
# every lib file carrying a mark imports internal/marks.
sngl check user_draw.sngl
stdout 'ok'

-- marks.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:internal/marks"

component main node {
    text(value="hi")
}

window {
    main
}
-- draw.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:internal/draw"

component main node {
    text(value="hi")
}

window {
    main
}
-- intrinsic.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:internal/marks"

#[intrinsic("my.thing")]
func evil(x int) int { return 0 }

component main node {
    var n int = 1
    text(value="{evil(n)}")
}

window {
    main
}
-- user_draw.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import "sngl:ui/draw"

component main node {
    draw.canvas(width=100px, height=100px) {
        draw.circle(cx=50, cy=50, r=20, style={fill=#f00})
    }
}

window {
    main
}
